name: Azor
overview: Azor is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, noted primarily as the son of Eliakim within the genealogical line leading to the Messiah. His mention in Matthew 1:13 situates him within the sacred ancestry that culminates in Christ. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Azor means "help," reflecting a common Hebrew meaning. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God, but it aligns with the tradition of meaningful biblical names. His name is explicitly recorded in Matthew 1:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Azor as the son of Eliakim, as inferred from Matthew 1:13, and as the father of Zadok, explicitly stated in Matthew 1:14. These relationships place him clearly within the Messianic lineage, connecting him to both his father and his son.
scriptureSignificance: Azor holds significance as a link in the genealogical chain of Jesus Christ, emphasizing the fulfillment of God's promise through the tribe of Judah. His presence in the genealogy underscores the historical reality and continuity of the Messiah's human ancestry. Though not prominent in narrative events, his role contributes to the foundation of Christ's royal and covenantal heritage.
